**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

The RENEWAL rule targets auto-renewal traps, and this Agreement has none:

- **No renewal mechanic at all.** A document-wide search for "renew" returns zero hits, as does "increase" — there is no renewal term, no non-renewal notice window, and no price-uplift language.
- **§ 2 (p0011)** creates an evergreen term running "until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6."
- **§ 6(a) (p0032)** gives either party — us included — termination for any or no reason on **fifteen (15) days'** notice whenever no Statement of Work is outstanding, plus a 15-day cure-based termination right in § 6(b).

That is at least as favourable as the preferred position: no automatic renewal, an exit far shorter than the 30-day preferred window, no multi-year lock-in, and no unilateral escalation right. Since the structure benefits us, no edit is warranted.

One rationale-level note (not a deviation): with no renewal pricing mechanic, any fee change must be agreed in each Statement of Work. If renewal terms are ever added in negotiation, we should carry in the 12-month renewal term and the lesser-of-CPI-and-3% uplift cap at that point.
